summary: This joint resolution nullifies the Bureau of Land Management's December 2024 Coastal Plain Oil and Gas Leasing Program Record of Decision by declaring it disapproved under the Congressional Review Act so it has no legal effect.

scores.thoughts: The bill uses the Congressional Review Act to nullify a BLM record of decision on oil and gas leasing. It contains no provisions that authorize, appropriate, or alter any federal expenditures or budget authority. Any indirect fiscal effects from future leasing revenues are outside the scope of the spending metric.
No tax rates, credits, deductions, or revenue provisions are mentioned or altered by the resolution.
The legislation addresses federal land management and energy leasing; it has no connection to health insurance, providers, or medical programs.
No firearms, Second Amendment, or regulatory provisions related to guns appear in the text.
The resolution concerns only a BLM leasing decision and contains nothing on visas, borders, or immigration enforcement.
No language addresses reproductive health services or abortion access.
Defense authorizations or appropriations are not addressed.

The bill disapproves a BLM Record of Decision governing the Coastal Plain (ANWR) oil and gas leasing program. Nullifying that decision removes restrictions on leasing and development, thereby reducing environmental constraints on fossil-fuel extraction in a protected area. This directly advances the pro-development, deregulation end of the spectrum.
No welfare, nutrition assistance, or entitlement programs are referenced.
The measure does not touch education funding, schools, or choice programs.
No controlled-substance or enforcement provisions are present.
Sentencing, policing, or corrections policy are outside the bill's scope.
Tariffs, trade agreements, and import/export rules are not addressed.
The resolution neither authorizes new spending nor enacts deficit-reduction measures.
No civil-rights or nondiscrimination language appears.
Foreign assistance programs are not mentioned.
Election administration and voting access are irrelevant to the bill.
Data privacy or technology regulation is not at issue.
Worker protections or union rules are not addressed.
Religious exemptions and civil-rights balancing are outside the bill's subject matter.
